utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Foro. If I could remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Domazet: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Foro. I'll continue with my questions. Madam, while you lived in Belgrade with your parents, given the fact that you were only 1 year old when you moved, and you remember that, which part of Belgrade did you live in and did you move within Belgrade at any time?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first place we moved to was the neighbourhood known as New Belgrade. My address was the Lenin Boulevard. I first moved when I started going to university. This might have been sometime back in 1982 or 1983. I then lived in a different neighbourhood behind the film city; that's on the opposite side of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "I lived, I started studying," I assume that you moved and lived with your parents and that the flat belonged to your parents?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that the first flat that you lived in and probably the next one, too, were obtained or given to you to use by the JNA, your father's employer?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This new relocation was probably to a bigger and better flat?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your parents stay in that second flat behind the area known as the film city all the way until 1991?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what became of that flat. Did your father eventually buy it or whatever happened?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A gentleman moved in, another JNA officer, who left Zagreb for Belgrade at the same time. He moved into that flat by force, which I only found out later after I'd been exchanged and when I arrived in Zagreb in late December and early January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's all very well, but my question is: What's the ownership? Does the flat still belong to your parents, no matter who happens to be living in it?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain what that means, that your father is not the owner or simply no longer resides there?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was never the owner of that flat. He didn't buy the flat because it was impossible under the law in the former Yugoslavia for JNA flats. You had tenancy rights and if you were the occupant of a flat those were the rights you enjoyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but those who had the tenancy rights were normally in a position to buy the flat normally at much lower rates than they would be on the open market and most people did just that. Are you absolutely certain that your father was not one of them?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm positive. At that time in the JNA you could only buy the flat off once you were about to retire and you were thinking that this was your last move.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but that was my understanding of our situation. Your father was about to retire.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the process of his retirement had begun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your mother have a job, too, during your stay in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My mother used to work while they still lived back in Vukovar. She tried to get a job in Belgrade. She kept trying for about ten years but consistently failed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, throughout your stay in Belgrade, in your case that amounts to about 23 years, you all lived off your father's salary?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, off my father's work, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that your parents moved in May 1991. Was that before or after the incident in Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, who is the question about? Can you please clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm pausing for the sake of the transcript. So my question was: You mentioned that your parents moved back to Vukovar in May 1991. Was that before or after the incident that you remember in Borovo Selo, which occurred in that same month?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was just before, perhaps days before. We were in the middle of the May holidays. Everybody was off work, and it was just before that that they had arrived back in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father arrived around holiday time in May. Did he ever go back to Belgrade after that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He continued to receive his JNA officer's salary, didn't he; and if so, how?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I think he was using cheques of some sort to withdraw his salary whenever it came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following their arrival in Vukovar, your father and mother continued to live off that salary; they had no other jobs?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My mother and father lived off their work their entire lives. You're talking about living off some salary or rather that they were receiving. My father earned that salary. He was a violin teacher and he worked with an orchestra for 35 years. He earned every penny. Every penny he got he earned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, when I was talking about his salary, obviously I don't mean getting money for nothing. It goes without saying your father earned his salary. I believe we understand each other quite well in fact, despite the appearances. But your mother was a housewife throughout, and I'm asking you, the situation was the same after they returned to Vukovar. Was the situation the same in terms of you living off that one salary that your father earned as a JNA officer?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only until the conflict broke out. After that point in time, you could no longer receive that salary. It lasted for maybe a month or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you about something else now. Do you remember that Croatia after the elections in December 1990 amended its constitution? Is this something you remember?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember it as a fact; the constitution was indeed amended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that after these amendments and the new constitution, Serbs in Croatia ceased to be a constituent group, as indeed they had been under the previous constitution? They were - to use a term widely used at the time - thrown out of the constitution; and this was actually the first time that tensions began to mount between the two ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say this yet again: I am no constitutional expert or lawyer, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you remember this as something that was a problem very much in the public eye at the time, especially for the Serbs? This was an important issue at the time, a much debated one, and also it was one of the things that triggered tensions in Croatia. Serbs were worried what would come of them after the constitution was adopted. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, I lived in Belgrade for 24 years. I never felt very constituent there myself, constituent in Serbia or constituent in terms of Yugoslavia. I am no expert. I am no constitutional expert, but in my understanding the constitution was in keeping with all the standards, constitutional standards, that prevailed in Europe at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the fact that the Serbs were thrown out, as it were, of the constitution? They were no longer even referred to in the preamble of the constitution as a constituent ethnic group living in Croatia. I think that applied much more to Serbs than it applied to Croats. I hope you will at least agree with that.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will agree that there weren't that many Croats living in Serbia. I'm sorry. What was the question, that the Serbs were thrown out? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, from the new constitution.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They weren't thrown out. You said it yourself after all, they ceased to be a constituent ethnic group in Croatia, that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about the National Guards Corps as a military unit, as the Croatian armed forces. You were able to see the members of the National Guards Corps yourself frequently. Can you tell me something about the sort of uniform that they were wearing, the sort of weapons that we were carrying, and who they got the weapons from?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately I can't answer all these questions, but I can answer the ones that I know. They were wearing camouflage uniforms and they had this check-board insignia which is also displayed on the Croatian national coat of arms and flag. I have no idea who they got their weapons from, nor did I ever want to know. But for the most part, they had light weapons, that is rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any heavy weapons in Vukovar, I mean heavier or more powerful weapons than the ones you've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that there were other weapons along the front line, but they were short of ammunition. They had mortars some sort, or at least that's what I heard at the time, not very powerful ones, and no ammunition to use. And they only fired very seldom for these reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have anti-aircraft weapons in Vukovar, for example?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I knew of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear or see that on the 24th of August that year, JNA air force plane was shot down right above Vukovar? It must be something you heard at the time, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about this, but I think people were saying that it hadn't been anti-aircraft weapons being used in order to shoot that plane down but something much simpler, a simpler kind of weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're suggesting the plane was shot down by something that was not an anti-aircraft weapon?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's what I heard at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they shoot down one or two planes on that day? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think two, but I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the weapons that the National Guards Corps had, you spoke about their uniforms with the chess board. Were they all wearing the same sort of uniform and was this a distinguishing feature between the ZNG and the police units that were in the area?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they all had uniforms, and those that did were ZNG members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how members were recruited by mobilisation, by compulsory mobilisation, or was there a different method being used?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was no compulsory mobilisation. People tended to join as volunteers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the fact that you were able to distinguish regular JNA soldiers from members of the Territorial Defence, especially based on how the latter often sported long hair and beards, unlike the JNA people. Could you also apply this to the ZNG, the National Guards Corps? Did their members also sport long beards and hair, or did they, much like JNA soldiers, have to be clean-shaven and orderly?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never noticed that ZNG members were anything less than orderly. They were, in fact, as orderly as was possible at the time under those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't take long hair and long beard to be something that is slovenly. I'm just saying ab the standards that were applied for a while. I wouldn't apply long hair and long beards as slovenly. I'm merely wondering if this was something allowed in the National Guards Corps because, after all, you had ample opportunity to see their members and you knew what they looked like?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said yourself that for a while it wasn't allowed to wear a beard in the JNA. Is it allowed now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sure that at the time it still wasn't.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then the answer is I didn't notice that the ZNG members were slovenly, poorly dressed, that they had long hair or sported beards. I noticed none of these. That's your answer. They certainly didn't go and get their hair-do's done regularly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what HOS stood for at the time?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know HOS are Croatian defence forces. I think that's what it stands for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Who were members of HOS and did they have an image of -- or rather, was Ante Paraga their chief?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never saw such individuals, the ones described by you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I never described them for you. I would like you to do that for us. I never saw them myself.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, you did describe them. You said what they wore and everything else. I never saw such people myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I never described them, Madam. I just inquired whether you knew about HOS and whether you knew about what that stood for. I never even attempted to describe their members. I want you to do that, and I want you to tell us what they wore.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw members of HOS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that throughout that time in Vukovar there were no members of HOS defending Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say is that I never saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your information, was that a paramilitary formation or regular military force, similar to the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you perhaps didn't know at the time, did you learn later or do you know now what I just asked you about the members?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned the Eltz castle, and as far as I know that was both a monument and a museum.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the castle of Count Eltz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Do you know that for a while the ZNG staff was housed precisely in that castle and that there were certain rockets positioned there as well as Rams, and that this was a target?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We mentioned the downing of planes in Vukovar; you remembered that event. Since another event happened at the same time, namely the event which took place at the cemetery when a JNA tank came by, can you tell us did this happen before or after the downing of the JNA planes?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't remember at all when the planes were shot down. I know that the event at the cemetery took place at the end of August. I remembered this very well because the JNA tank fired on civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took that date as the date from which further on there were no more funerals at the cemetery, so this is why I thought that perhaps you would be able to remember what date it was when it happened.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was either on the 25th or 26th of August, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So if the planes were shot down on the 24th of August, this is the information that I have, then that would mean that the planes were shot down before the cemetery incident. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's how it was, then that's how it was. If this is the information you have and if it's accurate, then yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have something else I want to ask you about the incident with the tank. You said that the tank moved and fired on civilians or in the direction of civilians. Was there infantry accompanying the tank or some soldiers or any other force moving with the tank, or was there just the tank there when it opened fire?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mostly tried to shield myself away from the tank fire, so I didn't really analyse it in detail. What I can confirm is that we spent two hours at the cemetery in a small house there, while the tank devastated all of the buildings around the cemetery. After we tried to escape, there were 10 to 12 of us, including families, the ones I've mentioned, those who got killed in the castle after -- I don't know what it was, whether it was shelling or whether the missiles were fired on the castle, but after that we started running towards the woods, the closest woods, next to the cemetery while the tank kept firing at us. I remember this well because the tank was firing on civilians. I didn't see anybody else but us there. The woods was apparently mined. The mines had been placed there, and we had to run through the woods to reach the nearest houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the tank destroyed some buildings, some houses at the cemetery. What kind of houses were there?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Morgue, morgue buildings. The bodies that had been brought in from the Eltz castle, once we left that building, which was in the depth of the cemetery, we could see that these bodies were destroyed by the tank grenades, including all of the buildings which were there, a morgue, the little house which served as a flower shop and also sold funeral accessories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that these people, after all, were not buried at the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that means that they were not buried and that they were blown to pieces and it was impossible to pick the pieces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know or do you know Alenka Mirkovic, a journalist in radio Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know her but I heard her reports on the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what was your view of her reports? Was it objective, unbiased, or not?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, she reported on the extent of the shelling in town, how many buildings were destroyed, how many civilians were killed. As far as I know, her reporting was unbiased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This lady as a radio journalist, somebody who reported on what happened, said the following, and maybe you'll remember hearing this on Radio Vukovar. She said that she managed to get to know the infamous HOS members who came to the ruined buildings and then immediately went to the positions in Sajmiste. It was so dangerous there that we had -- we didn't dare go there, nor did they have the time to come to our staff. It was said that they were quite unruly, that they listened only to Paraga, and that once they defended Vukovar they would head on to Zemun, and that they were called the killing machines. Later we heard that they -- later, once we heard that they referred to them as paramilitary formations, we were quite angered. Our HOS members held the most difficult positions in town. Do you remember hearing such reports and did you, in the meantime, remember that members of HOS were defending Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was that I had never seen any HOS members, and I stand by that. Sajmiste is not close to Mitnica. It is a part of the town, but Mitnica is at the exit of the town and Sajmiste is elsewhere, and never throughout the wartime did I visit Sajmiste. I think that on the map we showed that these are two different parts of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of what you said, can you rule out the possibility, or perhaps not, that members of HOS were positioned in Sajmiste and that they did constitute Vukovar defence?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only testify about what I saw. Anybody can make inferences that you're asking me to make now, anybody in the courtroom can do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time when the Mitnica staff was housed in the basement where you yourself where, did you know and can you tell us where the front line was, the one facing the JNA, on that side. Was it close to that location?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean where the utility company was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't close. The utility company was in the centre of Mitnica, and the demarcation line, if I can call it that, was near the houses which were closest to the new cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on that, one could say that this is where the front line was. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since there was a JNA tank near the cemetery and some other weaponry as well, as I heard later, then, yes, most likely it is that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it be said that Mitnica was the forward front line or the first one that one could encounter coming from the south?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could say so. That is how it was at the time, because all of the villages that had been occupied prior to that were places who residents had been expelled and sent to camps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was any direct combat, or was it mostly a case of artillery fire? You also said that there was an attempt by the JNA infantry to breakthrough. Do you remember when it was, if that is the case?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. I remember that they attempted this on three or four occasions, and that these attempts of the JNA infantry to breakthrough were repelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the surrender negotiations started, surrender of the ZNG members at Mitnica, you said yesterday that at the time there were about 180 of them. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 180 members of the National Guards Corps, the ZNG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, on the 18th of November. And what about the prior to that, during the combat that you described, there were probably many more of them then. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that none of the ZNG members withdrew and went into breakthrough, as they called it, leaving Vukovar before the 18th of November?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, nobody from Mitnica did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This figure of 180 members, how did you learn this, because this is something that only the top echelons could know, commanders; not even members of these units would know that figure?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that after the war I worked in the department which drew up lists and prepared material for the exchange of prisoners. This is what I learned at the time. All of the combatants who had surrendered their weapons were registered by the European monitors and International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you learned about this figure later on in Zagreb, and that's how you know this figure?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I learned about the exact figure later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said today and I think also yesterday that when the weapons were surrendered, the European monitors registered or recorded the names of people. How did they do that? Did you see this?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The surrender of weapons was taped on video. I saw these tapes later on. A member of the International Red Cross stood there and recorded names. I don't know how, but he just stood there and wrote down the names of the people surrendering weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you properly that you personally saw them as their names were being written down by representatives of the international community?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't go to the representative of the International Red Cross and watch what he was doing. I was some metres away, and I looked on as people handed in their weapons and a Red Cross representative was standing by and evidently taking down their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was whether you saw that personally or whether you heard about that later?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I saw it myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talked about the shelling and your visit to the hospital, if I understood you properly yesterday you went there in order to see your husband, because you said that you hadn't seen him for a while. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that you said that practically all the buildings you saw on your way to the hospital or on your way back from the hospital were, according to you, destroyed, demolished to their foundations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning you said that we speak similar -- a similar language, but obviously we do not understand each very well. I did not say that all the buildings at that time were demolished to the foundations. I said that the buildings were very much damaged, but they were completely destroyed in November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your description of the hospital which had been hit and quite considerably damaged would seem to indicate that the hospital was not destroyed in the same way that you described the other buildings being destroyed later. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the damage on the hospital building, but the hospital building was not completely destroyed at any point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean it was not completely destroyed? I don't understand really. I don't understand what you are trying to prove. It was damaged. It was shelled. It didn't have a roof. The walls were knocked down. It didn't have windows, and it was completely out of commission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talked about your departure from Vukovar and the column, you said that your parents were in a car and that there were also some other vehicles at the tail of the column and that you went to Ovcara all -- in these vehicles. Could you please tell us, during such shelling of the town and, as a result of the shelling, as you said, all the buildings were knocked down, how was it possible that the road that you were using and also on that day, how was it possible that you were able to go in a column in those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my yard of my family house, there were three vehicles and this is the only one that had survived. It was quite damaged, but it was working. You could ignite the engine and it was serviceable. The other two were completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talked about your departure and that you went to Sremska Mitrovica, for the first time yesterday you said something which you didn't mention in your statement. You said that you were in prison. You said yesterday that you were placed in a room, 90 of you, among whom there was an elderly woman, an old woman of 90, and also some children, one of them was 2 years old.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but I just have to correct you. In my statement that I provided in 1995, at the end of the statement I wrote that from Ovcara I was taken to Sremska Mitrovica where I spent 18 days and I was exchanged on the 5th of December. I don't know what you meant when you read that part of my statement, because in Sremska Mitrovica, it's obvious that that's not the place where there is a shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it's quite correct that you said that and that you were transferred to Sremska Mitrovica, that you stayed there for 18 days, but it wasn't said and even now it's not said that you were in prison because Sremska Mitrovica is a town in Serbia. It's perhaps the size of Vukovar, perhaps it's slightly larger. So Sremska Mitrovica is not only the penitentiary which is outside of town, so it could have been assumed that you were perhaps in some collection centre where there were other people such as you until the time of the exchange. The prison was not mentioned until yesterday. Is it possible that there was a room in this prison where it was possible for 90 people to be?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: People in a collection centre, people who live freely in a town do not get exchanged. Secondly, it's possible that the room was not meant to hold 90 people, but there were 90 of us in that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said for the first time yesterday that you were questioned several times during your stay there and that there was some others who were asked to give statements but not all. Can you please explain why some people were not called to make statements and you were called and asked to give a statement.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This 90-year-old grandmother was not asked for a statement, and neither was the child of 2. My mother was not asked to give a statement. At the time she was an older woman of 50, but all the younger people, all the women, were asked to give a statement -- actually, they were called for interrogation, and, during the interrogation they had to hold their hands on their back, they had to bow their heads and walk, accompanied by the police, to the interrogation room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the prison on the first day or second day after you arrived, you had a meeting with the rector of the university, and then after you had a meeting with the health minister of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, after you left the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you started to work on lists of missing persons and lists of victims. Did this only refer to the people who were missing from Vukovar, the people who were missing from the hospital, or missing persons generally throughout Croatia and perhaps even from Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our work mainly concerned people who were captured and disappeared from the entire territory of Croatia. At the time, the biggest humanitarian crisis was in Vukovar, so most of our work actually had to do with that part of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you worked on lists of missing persons and victims from the whole territory of Croatia. Did you work on such lists relating to people from Bosnia and Herzegovina or not?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall working on any material that had anything to do with Bosnia, except when we started to collect statements on violations of international humanitarian law from refugees who were accommodated in Croatia, so that amongst other things they testified about violations of international humanitarian law and crimes committed on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work on drafting a report to the commission of the Security Council, a report which Croatia handed in in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, to whom? To the UN?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did work on a part of it that referred to detainees, the missing persons, and generally the part that dealt with the humanitarian issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of what you said, were you also working on the problems of missing Serbs in Croatia, and is there anything about that in that report?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task was to collect statements from persons who were reporting missing persons. All those who came to the office to report a missing person were asked to give a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that the only source of your information for compiling those lists, the fact that family members came to report these persons, or was there another way?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the only source, contacts with persons who had survived certain crimes who were able to testify about them, and when families would come to report a missing family member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I take it then that clearly missing Serbs were not a part of your list?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can make or reach the conclusion that no Serb family members came to our office to report missing persons or to give a statement about events that preceded that or what happened to their family members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your office in Zagreb, you mean?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you say that you worked on a part of the report that Croatia sent to the UN commission, is it true that Yugoslavia -- the then-Yugoslavia sent the same report from Belgrade to the experts -- expert commission which was formed under the same resolution of the Security Council, and it was on missing persons from 1992? Did you have the opportunity to look at that report?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know that all the countries from the territory of the former Yugoslavia had sent such reports, but at the time I was very busy so I didn't really study those reports and it wasn't my job to do so. And also, in the report -- the -- my share on the work of the report that Croatia sent was very small and it related only to the humanitarian problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The report sent to the expert commission talks about Vukovar and the events in Vukovar a lot, even though the report encompassed events throughout Croatia, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and even Slovenia at the time that this was important there. I want to read just some things out to you to see if you had heard of that or if you have anything that you know about that in any way, perhaps while you were still in Zagreb or during the time you were in Vukovar or perhaps you had heard about that in some other way. Are you aware of an event in Borovo Naselje on the 4th of July, 1991, when Dragan Mijatovic and Stojan Stojanovic and some other unidentified Serbs were killed?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of an event on the -- of an event on the 13th of July, 1991, in Borovo Selo when two more Serbs were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned -- I see that my last question is not in the transcript, so I'm going to repeat it. It's an event of the 13th of July of 1991 in Borovo Selo when Milenko Djuricic was killed. He was arrested by two members of the ZNG. You mentioned the village of Sotin yesterday, which is next to Vukovar. Are you familiar with an event on the 29th of July in that village when Mihajlo Nadj was killed and that the possible perpetrators were three people, including Zdravko Komsic, whom you mentioned and you knew well, as you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear about those individual incidents, and I've already explained that to the Trial Chamber. I, in particular, don't know the names of all those persons. If you would like to continue to read that and explain that and if that is serving some other function other than the function of questioning a witness, I agree, but all the answers will be the same because I really don't know any names that you are talking about. I've already told you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Then I will not read anymore if you say that you don't know about any of the incidents. I'm not going to do that, but all I would like to say is that, in the report regarding the civilians in Vukovar and the environs, about 43 individuals are mentioned and the killings of over 100 Serbs, and this report was sent to the UN. But since you say that you don't know any of these individual events, I will not go on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, over 200 Serbs were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you yesterday if you knew Tomislav Mercep. You said that you heard of him but you didn't know much more about that. If I were to tell you that he was in charge of the defence of Vukovar at the time that the Secretariat for Defence was under his -- was under his care, then would you say that you knew anything about him?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you the same thing I already told you. I heard of Tomislav Mercep. I don't know had a his function was. I was never interested in that, and until 2005 I had never seen the gentleman face-to-face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see him perhaps in a television programme on Croatian television about Vukovar when he said that allegedly President Tudjman stated that it was more important to him to save 200 -- Zagreb citizens from getting killed than to spare 2.000 citizens from Vukovar from getting killed. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I generally avoided watching such television programmes because that only reminded me about the events that I had lived there, and it upset me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who was Pole Stipo?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, just before we move on that there's a correction page 23, the transcript line 19. It should read and -- it should read "than to spare 2.000 citizens of Vukovar."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, it is not quite clear what counsel is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question: Do you know who Pole Stipo is?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I apologise. One thing I would like to know: Will I be answering questions relating to my testimony, or will you spend the next following days asking me about the names of persons that I don't know and never referred to in my statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I'm asking you about both thing that you referred to in your statement and facts that might affect your credibility before this Court. That precisely is the reason why I am asking questions about certain people that I believe you would have had to know if indeed you were in Vukovar at the time and spent so much time there, and if it is your objective to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Again, I'm asking you: Pole Stipo, does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. I was 28 at the time. Politics was the least of my worries at the time. The people I knew were my friends and the people, the circle of people I had socialised with from a young age on. On the other hand, it's quite obvious that you're not asking questions about my statement -- my testimony. You are asking questions on assertions that you wish to be heard, but that has little to do with me and my testimony here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were to tell you that Pole Stipo was the commander of Vukovar's defence residing in the neighbourhood of Mitnica and that he was in that post in 1991, if I were to tell you that before the clashes he was the police commander in the Vukovar port authority at the Danube, would that ring a bell after all?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that gentleman. I never met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Ante Roso?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heard of but I didn't know the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I perhaps know what exactly you heard about him.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I heard of him. I remember his name. He was one of Vukovar's defenders, that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Marin Pliso?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was also one of Vukovar's defenders. The name certainly rings a bell. I believe he was a shop owner before the war, something like that, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on the information I have, he was an HDZ member and he was placed in charge of procuring weapons for the ZNG. But since you say you know nothing about that, well -- what about Ferdinand Jukic, nicknamed Jeja, or Develi Fati [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know all the names from Mitnica, the people who were at Mitnica. I told you I worked with lists of people later of people who were killed as well as the lists of those who were awaiting to be exchanged or who went missing in Vukovar. It's difficult for me to distinguish about the people I didn't know personally, whether I heard about their names back then or perhaps came across their names later on three years later when I worked with these lists of exchanged and missing persons. What I can confirm is anything in relation to those people who I knew personally and was in touch with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Ivica Franjic, nicknamed Pastor. His war nickname was Srna.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard his name or saw it on a list. It's difficult to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Ivan Soljic?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan Soljic spent some time in our cellar, in our shelter. He was with the National Guards Corps command. I knew him or was in touch with him at one point, meaning I talked to him. And I think he was killed just before Vukovar was occupied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The more you mention this occupation of Vukovar, the more I keep wondering what that means to you. Are you talking about the 18th of November or are you talking about an earlier date?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 18th of November. That was the beginning of the occupation, the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ivan Soljic, was he not a commander of the ZNG for Mitnica of all places? Did you hear about the 204th Brigade of the ZNG or battalion.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a legendary brigade because it was successful in Vukovar in repelling JNA attacks, and the JNA had superior weapons. They repelled their attacks and held them off for nearly four months. I think even Soljic at one time was its commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At Mitnica. Was he also perhaps the president of the Crisis Staff at Mitnica?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, for a while at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that after, that he remained in that position, the commander of the 204th, until the 12th of November, 1991? Can you confirm that since you were there?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that I was in the area, but I can't confirm that because I didn't go into these military matters, nor were they likely to share this sort of detail with us, and I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember how long you kept seeing him for there, in this place that was to all practical intents the headquarters of the National Guards Corps? My information seems to be suggesting that the 12th is six days before Vukovar eventually fell. Would that be possible? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is possible it was several days before the occupation of Vukovar or, rather, the entry of the JNA into Vukovar. That was when I no longer saw Mr. Soljic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What Mile Dedakovic was that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. He was the commander of Vukovar's defence at one point in time during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he perhaps the superior of this man whom we have just discussed, Ivan Soljic?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about how this worked, the hierarchy and everything, nor was I interested. The important thing was to survive. My curiosity was not much peaked by these details concerning the military hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you were spending days and nights in that cellar with the command staff of the National Guards Corps of Mitnica. Ivan Soljic was a commander there for a long time and Dedakovic was the overall commander of the Vukovar defence. I'm asking you was he his superior. You're saying you don't know. I'll ask my next question. At the time when you say you no longer saw Soljic, the reason was that Dedakovic had had him replaced and that's why he was no longer around?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that and I can't comment. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not say that based on your information Ivan Soljic was killed before the fall of Vukovar? Was my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In actual fact I was not familiar with his fate. It's just that at one point in time I stopped seeing him at the headquarters, where previously I used to see him regularly. I don't know what really happened to him. Speculation was rife, everybody was talking about it, but in actual fact I don't really know this for a fact. I assume that he was killed, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did writer tell you that several days before the fall of Vukovar after he was dismissed he fled Vukovar and went to Hungary and that he had already sent his family to Hungary earlier on, therefore he was safe and not killed. And seeing as you have no other information on the man's fate, would you agree that this was a possibility?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard stories, many stories, about Ivan Soljic, how he ended up in Zagreb. I heard all sorts of stories. I'm not sure what your information is based on. I'm not sure why your story would be more credible or trustworthy than other stories that I've heard, given that you don't seem to have any documents about what really happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you talked about his possible death before the fall of Vukovar. I'm telling you he survived. Do you have that sort of information?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were all sorts of accounts and rumours surrounding the fate of Ivan Soljic. There were several stories, but none substantiated, none more credible than the other. I don't think I can comment any further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But if I may just observe something. I asked many questions about what was going on in Vukovar, especially at the period of time when you were still free to move about and get on with your life as usual, but you didn't seem to confirm any other incidents save for the one in Borovo Naselje. And then you spent days and days on end in a cellar hardly ever leaving the cellar, and yet you were very accurate about describing where the shells were coming from and that how that plane suddenly emerged from behind the river. It's very difficult for me to verify what's true and what isn't, in view of all the things that you have testified about.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect to you, sir, I must point something out to you. Everybody suddenly gets extremely interested in what's going on once shells start raining down on you and falling on your head. You, too, would be very interested. You, too, would in no time at all learn what kind of missiles these were and how to take shelter and save your life in the face of these missiles falling on top of you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no doubt about that, Madam. I'm just saying that you provided information that could only have been obtained by careful and close observation, whereas you did not actually witness these things yourself. As for the period while you were still free to move about, your powers of observation didn't seem to be that sharp. But let's not pursue that any further. I would like to conclude by asking you something which I think says a lot about your attitude to this Court in some of the answers you have given. At the very beginning of your transcript, page 1 of yesterday's transcript, my learned friend from the OTP asked you about your personal information. You said you completed primary school and secondary school in Belgrade, started studying, and graduated. That's fine. However, I have information that you had five exams to go at the time you quit university, which you confirmed. However, you had completed all your courses, you had completed the four compulsory years of university, and you only had five exams to go before you obtained your diploma at the pharmaceutical faculty. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I spoke about my studies, I said that I had nearly graduated, nearly graduated. I think my statement is very clear about that. I have no reason to be saying that I graduated if, in fact, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what the transcript says, and had I not asked the question now it would have remained that way. However, that is not my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, can I make it clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- that the effect of the evidence yesterday as the Chamber understood it was very clearly that the witness had not graduated. She had stopped in her course five examinations short of completing the course. So if --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- there is some error in the transcript, it's not one that affected the sense of her evidence yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] She did answer my question when I asked the question about the five exams, but on page 1, line 18 and line 19: [In English] "I completed primary and secondary school and started studying at university in Belgrade and I graduated."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but I didn't say that. It's that simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You set the record straight saying that you completed the four years and that you only had five exams to go before your diploma?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never pronounced the word "I graduated." I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Fair enough. We know nothing about that, whether it's true, that you had indeed completed the four years of studies and you only had five exams to go. I have better information to corroborate that. But I have a list of students of the pharmaceutical faculty in Zagreb 2001, the academic year 2001 and 2002, number 17 reads "Sarlota Fora taking the third year of the course for the second time," and the same information applies to 2003. You, yet again, had to repeat this same year of the course, the third year. Can you confirm this information, and how different is this from you completing the four years in Belgrade and just nearly graduating, as you said.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. If you go back and check the way the system worked, the education system, you will see that the programmes are quite different in Zagreb and Belgrade respectively, via curricula. When I finally obtained or retrieved my documents, university documents, from Belgrade, on account of the differences in the respective curricula, I was sent back to my third year in Zagreb with the differential exams still to be taken. So much for the education system and its consistency throughout the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But you didn't tell us about that. When you spoke about continuing in Zagreb, you didn't say that you had to go back a year or two.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You never asked me about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but I just wanted to clarify and comment on everything you stated here before this Court. I thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Domazet. About 20 minutes -- we're speeding up the team before you, Mr. Borovic. You've got about 20 minutes' clear run now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Borovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Borivoje Borovic, I am Defence counsel of Miroslav Radic in this case. My first question: Immediately upon leaving prison, you went to Zagreb and were given a job there. My question is: One year of experience at a level of a low clerk in a small town in Croatia seemed to be a sufficient recommendation for getting a job in the Ministry of Defence. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until 1992 we were not officially employed nor did we receive remuneration for our work. This was a pro bono, voluntary work. Later on I found a job at the medical school, where I started collecting documentation that I described to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But you didn't answer my question. Was this recommendation of a one-year experience at a level of a low clerk in a small town in Croatia, was that a sufficient recommendation or were you, in fact, recommended by your war experience?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anybody who wanted could have gotten the job that I did. My -- what recommended me was that I knew what had happened in Vukovar. I was able to identify the people who had to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you knew everything that happened in Vukovar, we're now going to cover that one by one. You said that you knew of Mercep. My question is: Do you know that on the 8th of August he issued permits limiting the movement of citizens around Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never needed any permits when I went to any part of the city after the 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As my colleague before me said, based on our information it was only the members of the ZNG who didn't need such permits. Everybody else needed them. Does that mean that you were a member of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that doesn't mean that, and it is clear that your information is not accurate, seeing that I was there and not you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the information about permits, I gained this information through the testimony of various witnesses testifying here before you, witnesses who were well familiar with this. My next question is: What areas were under your control in the month of September? When I say "your control," I'm referring to the following: Yesterday while giving testimony you said -- you frequently referred that such-and-such an area was under our control. Therefore, I'm asking you now: What areas were under your control in September?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only testify about the area where I was. Mitnica was mostly under the control of Croatian defenders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From when to when?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From when I asked.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already explained, for me the beginning of an open conflict was when the tanks passed and opened fire in Mitnica. That was in late August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you didn't answer my question. From what time on was Mitnica under the ZNG control?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I did answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I didn't understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Open conflicts erupted in late August, whereas the surrender of weapons and civilians -- evacuation of civilians was on the 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to visit your husband in the post office, as you testified yesterday, through which areas of Vukovar did you have to go? What are these areas of Vukovar called from Mitnica to the post office?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Mitnica one reaches the centre of the town. I would take the main road to the centre of the town. And after that, I would take the main road to the hospital. So all of that can be deemed the centre of the town, Mitnica and then the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the after the hospital?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go anywhere beyond the hospital. I don't know what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, did you go to visit your husband?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's before the hospital. You probably didn't pay close attention to the map that I drew. We have Mitnica, then the centre of the town, post office, and then comes the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these areas under the control of the ZNG at the time when you went to the post office?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA didn't enter the centre of the town prior to occupation, which came, as I said, on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you are a witness who is supposed to give us accurate information and answer the questions put to you, please tell us: Do you know whether at the time the ZNG had the centre of Vukovar under their control? Did you see there formations which, according to Defence, were paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: While Vukovar was defended, I never saw any paramilitary formations. I saw members of the ZNG, meaning Croatian army. I've already answered your question, namely that the JNA as the attacking army, the army that shelled the city, didn't enter the centre of the town until Vukovar fell and was occupied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But you keep refusing to answer my question. Please do not interrupt me. You went from the headquarters of the ZNG in Mitnica to the hospital, and en route did you see any military positions of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any military positions of the ZNG. Most likely, positions were held elsewhere but not on the main street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where would that be, elsewhere, since you were in Vukovar and you are testifying here?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The positions were near the demarcation line where the JNA attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those were? You are the witness here. You passed through that area. Please do not interrupt me. Let me finish my question. So these were the lines from which the JNA attacked, as you say. You explained the weapons that they used. You saw the weapons that they fired from. You saw what they hit. So please tell us: Where were these lines? You are the witness.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified about the location of the line in the area where I was at Mitnica. In the centre of the town, there was no front line, nor demarcation line, on the main street or main road of the town, nor were there any ZNG units positioned there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But your answers are not of the kind that could impress the Defence. You seem to give hostile answers to very simple questions. I put a very simple, fair question to you. Did you see any ZNG members on the -- in that stretch, in that area, or not?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw individual persons wearing uniforms moving about town. I would see them very seldom. I saw maybe two or three because the shelling was in progress. And as I have already told you, I was driving in a car with a member of the ZNG who was taking his wounded colleague to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you first learn that there were 180 members of the ZNG at Mitnica? When was the first time you learned of that figure?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The list that we compiled, the list of the persons who surrendered their weapons, had 180 names of the persons who surrendered at Mitnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how many members were there three months earlier, since you were with the ZNG staff at Mitnica, you lived together, spent days and nights with the members of the ZNG staff, so did you ever hear of the number? How many were there at Mitnica?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already told you, there were 2 to 4.000 of us civilians there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to finally start answering my questions. I never asked you anything about civilians.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you say "you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I say "you," I meant you, members of the ZNG, since you lived in the headquarters of the ZNG which is a military facility. It is unlikely that a civilian would be able to live there.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, I am going to interrupt for two reasons. The first is that there is no suggestion in the evidence that this witness was a member of the ZNG. You are putting that as a fact -- as a preface to a question. The second is that I made a mistake earlier, and in my mind when you commenced I thought we were going to finish at a quarter to 11.00, but I was wrong and I'm sorry. So we will need to finish now because of the tapes, and we will resume, therefore, at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Among the ZNG members at Mitnica, were there any foreign nationals?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not a single one. I didn't see one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the headquarters there, was there a radio there or did they have radio equipment?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had communication equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they communicate in your presence with the hospital via that equipment?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. We mostly didn't listen to the conversations they had because a majority of them were confidential.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you attend the meetings of the staff when decisions were adopted?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we conclude, in view of the fact that the Main Staff was present there at Mitnica, that the utility company was transformed into a military facility?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you can conclude. What I told you was that the staff was housed in the basement because the building where they had been prior to that was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And where was that where they were housed prior to that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. It was somewhere in Mitnica near the small post office or in that vicinity, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what a shell fired by a multi-barrelled rocket launcher looks like?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and describe it?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks like a rocket. It leaves a fire trace or trail behind it, and upon contact with the ground it disperses everywhere. Unfortunately I had occasion to get personally acquainted with such shells fired by multi-barrelled rocket launcher when it killed several people and when these shells started landing all over around the area where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you describe a mortar shell for us, please.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, a mortar doesn't fire shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what does it fire?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like a grenade or something similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please describe this similar object that you testified about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I testified about detonations caused by mortar ammunition. I didn't study this ammunition. What I can tell you is that there were detonations of different intensity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you distinguish the shells based on their sound? Can you make a distinction between an artillery shell, a missile fired by a multi-barrelled rocket launcher, and a mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They all caused different detonations. When a multi-barrelled rocket launcher fired a grenade, then that produced several consecutive detonations of various intensity. And they differed from the detonations caused by a shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you ever see a mortar grenade being fired and landing?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I seen this personally, I would not have been able to talk to you now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, had you ever seen it?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the rocket fired by a multi-barrelled rocket launcher, did you see it in its flight and when it landed?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that at Mitnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your impression?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A very unpleasant one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Did you ever see a multi-barrelled rocket launcher? And if so, would you please describe it to us.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it when we went to Ovcara. Once you turn from the main road to Sotin, when you turn to Ovcara, that's what I described yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you ever see it prior to that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able to explain to the Court how come you know what a rocket fired by a multi-barrelled rocket launcher looks like if you have never seen it before and if you have no military experience?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no military experience, and you yourself would quickly learn had you been in a situation where such shells were raining down upon you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you went to the hospital two or three times and you described that one occasion. What was the reason for you on the other two occasions to go to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to meet my husband.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber why you passed by your husband and went to the hospital. That's not the same reason, because if the post office is before the hospital, then why go to the hospital? Was there any particular reason for that? It seems to me - you can help me - but the way you explained it the post office is on the way to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. We were transporting the wounded. It was an urgent thing, so it was much more urgent to get them there and I was just there for the ride. So it was more important to drop them off at the hospital than me at the post office. I would walk back later to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then how did you go back to the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I walked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your husband ever visit you at the staff?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would come once a week or once every two weeks when it was possible, in view of the fact that movement was limited at the time. I'm talking about a three-month period now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The period from the 12th of October, did he ever visit you or not, from that time until the end?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What happened on the 12th of October?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you told us here, that on that day he left the post office and moved to live at your parents' place.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't on the 12th of October, but it was on the 12th of November. And in the original statement that I signed, it states the 12th of November in English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Listopad? Is that the tenth or the eleventh month?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it says "Listopad," then obviously the translation is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you read the English version of your statement the last time?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came here to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why are you making that correction in the addendum that goes with your statement, that you're only correcting it now?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because in the English that is correct. That is the original version which I signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I just wanted to tell you that in the B/C/S version it doesn't say the tenth month or the eleventh month, it says "Listopad." This is a specific name for a month in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think this is a mistake by a translator of this Tribunal. I have nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Did you enter the hospital on each of the occasions, of the three occasions?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then why did you go to the hospital? How far did you get?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the main entrance or the side entrance?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the main entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than arriving at the front entrance, did you go around the hospital? Did you walk around there or not?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the promenade was closed. I've already said that the shelling was incessant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
