utterances.text: My question was very specific. Did you stand around the front entrance or walk around the side of the hospital promenading?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not promenading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a very important question. Where did you see the sign of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was hung on the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the front side of the hospital building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where? Which part of the front of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Above the main entrance?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several entrances. The main entrance or what I considered to be the main entrance is the gate of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not speak at the same time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was at the widest part of the building. There was a large kind of flag on the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the sign I saw at the time because I was on that side.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. That was the first time that you came. And what about the second and the third time? Was the sign still there?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you stay at the main gate or did you go up to the building itself?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once I came out of the car at the main gate I went back towards the post office right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So that means that you did not enter the yard of the hospital from any side?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the gate of the hospital from where you can see the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. How can you then explain your conclusion to a question by the Prosecutor that there were no weapons of any kind in the hospital or around the hospital if all that you saw of the hospital was from the gate or if you were only at the gate?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't -- the part that I saw -- that's how I understood the question: Did I see any weapons in the area that I was able to see, and I did not. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So that only covers the area that you were able to see. During this three-month period were you in telephone contact with your husband?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were able to talk on the telephone very rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the last time that you talked like that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps in early November, and after that the lines were cut. And then after that he came to Mitnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the post office in the area controlled by the ZNG, you used to go there?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The post office was in the centre of the town, and I've already said that the Yugoslav People's Army did not have control on that -- in that part of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would agree that the ZNG had control in that area of the city?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Croatian army did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the Croatian army," do you also include the civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a very clear difference between armed soldiers, armed -- the army and the civilian protection. I've already explained that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But you did not explain that. Your husband you said joined the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that he did not get a uniform but that he was at home where he lived and that is where he performed guard duty in order to possibly prevent the JNA or the paramilitary forces from entering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he supposed to prevent them with his bare arms or did he have weapons?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had weapons but didn't have ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What weapon did he have?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And no ammunition?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little bit of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No ammunition or a lot of ammunition --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's start again. Your husband, a member of the civilian protection, had a rifle. How much ammunition did he have or did he have any ammunition at all?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had some ammunition, a little, just like everybody in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that or did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And your father, as a member of the Yugoslav People's Army, did he have a rifle in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those who went to perform guard's duty at these positions when they went from their homes, when they went on guard duty they would receive a rifle and then they would give it back once they returned home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did they get it from and who did they return it to?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. This was organised by the civilian protection command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the main commander of the civilian protection? Under whose command were your husband and your father?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They never told you that, not even after the war?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you allow for the possibility that Mercep was their supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would not allow for that possibility because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's a good answer also. Can you explain to us who was guarding your husband's mother because she was alone -- well, I hear that your husband was taking care of your parents. Who was taking care of his mother? Who was guarding her?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not guarding my parents. My father was also in the civilian protection. All those in Vukovar who were able to were part of the civilian protection. Since the -- my husband's family house did not have a cellar where you could be -- which you could use as a shelter. She went to her neighbour's. It was a fairly large cellar there. It was also quite full of neighbours who were living there so that in any case she was not alone. She was with his aunt and with all the other neighbours who were at that particular shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps this is not something of interest to the Defence, but is it logical -- wouldn't it be logical to invite that woman to come over and join your parents so that your husband could look after her as well, or perhaps you're not speaking the truth about the civilian protection positions where your husband and father were.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the beginning of my testimony here I have been speaking the truth. We did invite my husband's mother, but, however, she did not want to go too far from her house. She wanted to keep an eye on what was going on with her house. That was something, if you allow, that was important to her at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Earlier you stated that your husband while he was working at the post office would come home once a week or perhaps once or twice in the course of a week or two weeks. My question is: Does that mean that at the time he was sleeping at the post office?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what it means. We were all sleeping at shelters at that time because movement was restricted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he eat at the post office? Where did he have baths? Where did he sleep? How many people were there at the post office? Do you know anything about these things?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's logical to me because this is something that I lived there, something like that. Obviously you have no idea what you are talking about, with all due respect. Excuse me, all 10 or 15.000 people who happened to be in Vukovar at that time lived, had baths, and ate in shelters. They slept in shelters and they would go out only when it was necessary, and that is when they got killed. You're talking about a period when every third citizen of Vukovar was killed; two survived and one was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would just like to ask you not to raise your voice because you, as a witness, really cannot convince me in view of your statement that everyone was in the civilian protection who was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, that sort of comment is inappropriate. There's an antagonism going on between you and the witness which is not useful for the purposes of this hearing. We can get to the essential issues of the evidence in a quite orderly fashion. Your comment then and a number of others have not been assisting that. So if you would please ask your questions and not make personal comments about the witness or on the answers, and we will get along more quickly and more effectively. Your Defence case will be pursued more effectively if you can do it that way, and I'm sure other counsel will take notice of that comment because it's something that is a habit of several counsel. It will be a lot better for everybody if we deal simply with questions, get answers, and move on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next question. Besides automatic weapons and mortars that you talked about, do you know that the ZNG also had the support of artillery from Vinkovci?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I didn't have such information nor later, information of a military nature. I wasn't interested in that kind of information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As a daughter of the officer of the JNA, how was it that you earned the opportunity to spend time at the Main Staff of the ZNG at Mitnica? Did you go through any checks?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if anybody or who could have run a check on me. I knew most of those people from childhood. They probably came to my family house. How did I come to earn that was probably just by being in Vukovar at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated yesterday that their -- that they, meaning the Serb Territorial Defence, constituted a paramilitary force. I would like to ask you the following: And was your civilian protection a paramilitary formation? This is a very precise question.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be a little bit closer to such a conclusion if you say they do not have uniforms, there are no insignia, so is that then a military or a paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I explained in any case is that already all of those so-called units or groups of people who were in the civilian protection units or civilian protection groups were in the area and organised in the area where they lived. So they lived there, they were there as civilian protection for their own houses and their own families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And what do you think the Serbs did in the Territorial Defence? Do you have an opinion about that? Did they fight for their --

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what those two bearded men were doing together with Mr. Sljivancanin at Ovcara, but perhaps we don't need to talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the Trial Chamber, nevertheless, to warn the witness to start to answer my questions because I think that the way she is addressing us is not appropriate, regardless of where she was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is: What were the TO -- the Serb TO in Vukovar fighting for? Were they also fighting for their houses? That is the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is a new question. It is not at all like the question that you did put, which sought an opinion, Mr. Borovic. I just am putting that so that you will understand that you may have one thing in mind, but what you often put is different. And that doesn't -- what you do put is answered as best the witness can, and I really don't know how she could give an opinion on the subject that you did put to her, but when she does her best that way, you are then concerned that she hasn't answered the question that was in your mind rather than the question that you actually put. So if you can keep that in mind as well, there will be less frustration between you and the witness and we can move along.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I believe my learned friend has something to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. As my learned Defence colleague has been continuing, and indeed the entire Defence, with their cross-examination, I've tried not to raise as many objections as perhaps would ordinarily be the case, because, in my submission, the Court is having full control of the proceedings. However, I have noticed that apart from the observations Your Honour has been making that there are three Defence teams and a number of the questions are of a repetitive nature such as: Where was your husband working? And these have all actually been answered before by the witness in chief. And I think it may be more expeditious to the proceedings if perhaps we could address new areas as each counsel comes along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Agha. The Chamber has been discussing the progress of this case, and it proposes at a convenient time to put a number of issues to counsel, including the range of questioning, both by Prosecution and Defence. In the Chamber's view, there is a lack of attention to what are the material issues, a lot of attention to matters that really are of no significance at all. And there is a deal of repetition of questioning. But this isn't the time for us to delay on that. Carry on, please, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Might I provide a brief comment in relation to what my learned friend has just said, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At the appropriate time, Mr. Borovic. We don't want to waste time now. I have indicated to Mr. Agha that we'll be dealing with this topic at a convenient time later. So if you could leave your comment until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine, Your Honour. Fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that everybody was involved in the town's defence, including medical staff. Isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My personal opinion is that Vukovar was defended by all its citizens, by all those who remained there throughout. I never stated that medical staff were involved in the town's defence. If I said so, I did not mean that they were carrying weapons. They were involved in the town's defence by doing their own work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 18, line 6, you stated just that yesterday. I made a special note of that when you said that medical staff, too, were involved in the town's defence. However, you've just provided an explanation, and we are satisfied now. Did you meet Vesna Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was only in Sremska Mitrovica, but prior to that we were not personally acquainted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Vesna Bosanac before you arrived in Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw her as a doctor at the Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think probably back in 1991 and 1990. She was a paediatrician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Why were you at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw her because I had several different reasons to go to the hospital: I was ill myself, my husband was ill, when my father's father died, my father-in-law died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she ever come to the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mile Dedakovic come to your headquarters at any time?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw him there myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where the ZNG headquarters was for Vukovar? Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not positive, but I think it was either in the police building or somewhere else. I'm not sure, really. I think the police building, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred yesterday to a veterinary clinic. Was this in an area that was under ZNG control, the area around the veterinary clinic?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is in the settled area and I said that the confrontation line was at the far end of Mitnica where the last houses were facing the new cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said there were 180 ZNG members in your area, but you also said that all able-bodied men were members of the civil protection. How many members did the civil protection have at the time?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think anybody can tell you. I never heard a specific number. This was a self-organised thing. People joined the civil protection in their own areas, and it was based on streets, actually, and they defended their own homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a while ago that was it was an organised thing, that they were given weapons and they returned weapons. You know how it worked. Given the fact that they were given weapons and returned weapons, who kept those lists of weapons? Did anybody keep records and did anybody know how many weapons they had, more than the ZNG or less?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why it seems to you that I should be able to answer that question. It's not part of my experience. It's not part of my testimony. I can't provide this number. You may find it important, but I'm just unable to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, you're a witness and you said yourself that the civil protection was an organised affair. Since we have not, so far, been able to obtain this sort of information from anyone and you were the first to mention it, we just wanted to know if you can tell us more about how many members they were and how exactly they were organised. If it was based on streets and if people defended their own streets, if that's all you can say, I accept that, and thank you. What were you wearing at the time? Were you wearing a uniform, too?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that all the buildings were damaged. In late November the buildings around the hospital, based on what you knew, had already been razed to the ground. That's what you say. My question is: Was the MUP building, the police building, also flattened in late November?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. It was severely damaged, and the same applied to all buildings in that area. I did not go to the hospital after the 1st of November, therefore I can only speak about what it looked like earlier, after a three-month period of continuous shelling at Mitnica. That's the only thing I can speak about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified about those buildings around the hospital. What about the MUP building? Was it merely damaged or entirely flattened, as you told my colleague, Mr. Domazet? I think these are two different categories, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is the first question you asked about the MUP building, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you a question about that, but my colleague, who examined you before I started. In answer to his question you said the buildings were flattened, which means there was nothing left standing. I am just saying this to cross-check the answers of another witness, to be fair. So if you know, can you please describe the appearance of the MUP building on the 1st of November -- or rather, the last time you saw it.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In early October or mid-October, I went there for the last time. My impression was that all the buildings had sustained a severe degree of damage. Some had been flattened, but this is the first time that you yourself have referred to the MUP building specifically. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So what can you tell us about the MUP building? Was this one of those buildings that had been flattened, razed to the ground, or not?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was severely damaged. There was no roof, and the walls were severely damaged. It could not longer be used for its purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When your father left Belgrade, did he bring a weapon along?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he return his uniform and regulation, standard-issue weapon that he had before he left Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. How am I supposed to know something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before your evacuation that you have described, had you ever been to Ovcara and when?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had. As a child I would go there. We cycled around the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as a child you say. That was the last time you had been in the area prior to your evacuation?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the map that the OTP showed you which you marked. Was it yesterday that you saw that particular map for the first time or did you see that particular map earlier on?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen maps of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking about this particular one. Was yesterday the first time you saw it?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by earlier. When earlier? I'm sorry, but you'll need to specify. When specifically when you say "earlier." I've seen a great deal of Vukovar maps. I lived there and later on I dealt with these maps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will be patient enough to ask the same question for the third time. The map that you used and marked yesterday in the courtroom with a red highlighter, did you ever see that map before; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OTP showed me that map and asked me whether I could mark on this map my location during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When and where?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before my testimony, when we spoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you at that time also mark the same spots that you marked here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The JNA breakthrough at Mitnica, you say that many JNA soldiers were killed when they tried to achieve a breakthrough at Mitnica. Do you know exactly how many of their soldiers were killed, the JNA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many ZNG soldiers were killed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there were casualties on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are at this time living within the headquarters of the ZNG for Mitnica. Did you have that information about their casualties or not?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like to go back to that map. Did you use a red pen also when you talked to the OTP to make the same markings that you made in the courtroom? Was it marked in red? Or how was it marked?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just indicated the places that the OTP wanted to know about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the reason then why you took no time getting your bearings with the map when you saw it in court yesterday, because you saw the map previously and used it to mark all these spots the day before you appeared in court. Was that the reason?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're stating a fact there. I'm not sure I can see a question there. We're talking about a map of a place of which I was a resident. I lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will not be pursuing this any further. I think your position is crystal clear. Back in Sremska Mitrovica you provided three statements. Were all these three statements signed by you?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so because that's what the officer demanded, the officer who requested that I give these statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know the name of this officer who interrogated you three times?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you signed these statements -- well, first of all, my apologies. Did you write your own statement, physically write it, you?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I handwrote the statement myself. There was no typewriter or anything -- any other piece of equipment to use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who Dr. Njavro is?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a doctor, a surgeon I believe, from the Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When is the last time you saw him?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the anniversary of Vukovar's occupation on the 11th -- on the 18th of November, 2005.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you marked the anniversary of Vukovar's occupation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you discuss with the doctor what had happened in Vukovar in 1991 on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at this anniversary?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We just exchanged greetings, but we did not speak after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how many employees the Vukovar Hospital had in November?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If I tell you that there were about 350 employees there in November, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said I'm not familiar with that. I'm not sure why I should agree or disagree with you on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The times you went to the hospital, did you see any security at the entrance?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came, shells were falling all the time. It was very dangerous. You didn't linger at the entrance. There wasn't anyone there as far as I noticed, and I certainly didn't see any armed persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were standing outside waiting for those people to come back, those who were carrying the wounded?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't stand there waiting. I drove up. I did what I had to do, and I drove straight back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Bozidar Zugec is that a name that rings a bell?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a close family friend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Emil Aleksandar?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another close friend. They all worked at the post office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Defence has information that they were in charge of liaison between the post office and the ZNG at the time. What would you say about that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they were in charge of setting up communications with the rest of Croatia, between Vukovar and the rest of Croatia. It was later in my office that I saw emails, messages, that had been written personally by Mr. Aleksandar and Mr. Zugec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But did they have any military assignments during the Vukovar operation?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by military, but they didn't have weapons and they were not actively involved in combat. They were in charge of maintaining our communication lines with the rest of Croatia. I saw that they sent on information on the numbers of dead and wounded in Vukovar, as well as the lists of those people who had either been killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your husband have any tasks had those areas, since he also worked at the post office, especially after they moved into the basement?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody who worked at the post office at the time was involved in servicing or maintaining these communication lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Does your father receive his retirement benefits now?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon returning to Croatia, upon being exchanged, he became an active serviceman in the Croatian army. He became a member of an orchestra within the Croatian army and then retired from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many years did he work for the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think for about two years because he was quite ready for retirement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what about your husband, where did he work?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My husband also worked in the data processing. He was into software, computers, and so on. He did that within our office, and following that he went to work for the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Do you know who shot down the two JNA planes that were already described in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was done by the Vukovar defenders. They shot down the planes who had bombed the city -- which had bombed the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know what they used to shoot down the planes? Was it pistols, rifles?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I wasn't present and I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Foro, good morning to you as well. My name is Novak Lukic, and on behalf of the Defence team of Veselin Sljivancanin I will be putting questions to you now. I will be mostly exploring the topics covered by you yesterday in your examination-in-chief. You mentioned my client quite frequently. However, at the outset I will put some other questions which are important for Defence and which have to do with persons that you could tell us something about, since, according to our information, these people were your neighbours from Mitnica. Zeljko and Zeljka Duvnjak, do these names mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last name sounds familiar. There was several families with that last name, but I can't put a face to that name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was told that Zeljka is a sister of Loburic called Max. Does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Franjo nicknamed Brada, shopkeeper?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And what is the last name?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't have information on the last name. All I have is the nickname, Brada. He was a shopkeeper.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Mandic, Slobodan? He was a driver who worked for Veletrgovina?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I knew some other people with that last name, but not Slobodan Mandic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let us see if we can cover this quickly. If you know, fine; if not, let us proceed. Covic, the vet. I think his first name was Domagoj or something similar?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ivica Boskovic?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Kasalo brothers, Ivica, Nikola, and Drago?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know them. They lived at the end of the street where my house was. I know Ivica Kasalo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of ZNG? Did he take part in the defence of the city?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Ivica Kasalo was a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Matkovic, Ivica, was that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question pertaining to your neighbours. Do you know where the house of Dr. Crevar was located?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the house of Dr. Crevar was by the water-tower, if we have the same person in mind. He was a gynaecologist. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't have such information. All I know is that this is where the prison where Serbs was located. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have already heard you giving an answer to this question, but always linked to other questions. Yesterday you described the day when Mitnica surrendered and when all other events happened, including Ovcara. What date was it?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's precisely what I wanted to hear you say. Now, could you please go back to that period of time and tell me whether during that time you heard the name of any other JNA officer except for my client? Did you meet any other JNA officer?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to admit that I can't remember all the names that I heard. Perhaps I did hear some other names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you remember my client?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we met. That's why I remember him. I didn't meet any other senior JNA officers, and Mr. Sljivancanin introduced himself to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But as we heard yesterday, his name is something that you had heard even before meeting him. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. His name was mentioned in connection with negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the his face? Was his face also familiar to you even before you met him?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you remember seeing him there during the surrender of weapons, and later on that same man came up to you, introduced him as Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now briefly cover with you the time sequence, time-line of events you testified about. I will bring you through it quickly and I will ask you to just confirm whether this is true or not. Your negotiators left in the morning?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be more specific about the time of the day. When did they leave the headquarters to go to negotiate?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- in the morning about 8.00 or 9.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then they returned at around noon?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then they said that all of you had to be in front of the veterinary station an hour at the latest. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, this took some time. It took some time for people to gather there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how long did it take?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it took perhaps two hours. There was a column of civilians, column of troops, so it took some time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were two columns of people?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then from there you head towards the new cemetery?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there, at that spot, the defenders of the city, as you call them, surrendered their weapons, which was between 14 and 1500 hours. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was still daylight when they surrendered weapons. It was still daytime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there, as they surrendered weapons, you saw representatives of the International Red Cross and European mission listing the names of persons surrendering weapons. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At around that time you also saw Cyrus Vance monitoring and observing the surrender of weapons?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He stood to the side, separate from the group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all of that took place during daytime while it was still daylight, so sometime after 1400 hours? Could it be then?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because in November it gets dark at around 4.30 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But it was still daylight?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then those who had surrendered weapons were taken away as well as a large number of civilians who were not in vehicles, such as you, they were taken somewhere?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were taken from that spot, soldiers who had surrendered weapons, and the column started moving along so that after the curve near the cemetery they boarded the buses which, according to what I learned later, went to Croatia or to some prisons in Serbia. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you remained there by the cemetery in your vehicle waiting until the evening, 21 or 2200 hours?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The evacuation was in progress during that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, escorted by a military vehicle, you travelled to Ovcara for some 20 minutes. And, according to what you told us yesterday, you arrived in Ovcara between 22 and 22.30. It was already dark?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It was already late in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described what us what happened in Ovcara, but you didn't tell us when, in your estimate, you left Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed in Ovcara for about an hour. I don't know how it took, maybe an hour and a half. I don't know how long it took for that entire procedure to be completed, the one I described. Perhaps it took about an hour and a half all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you after all this time to be more specific than that. Then finally you said that on the following morning at around 2.00 you arrived in Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was very early that morning, at 2.00 or 3.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described to us yesterday the situation in which you saw Cyrus Vance. That was the first time you ever mentioned that incident. You didn't mention it previously when giving statement to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave my statement to the investigators in 1995, and we didn't go into details about the Mitnica surrender. We didn't bring up the details. The focus was for me to say that I was at Ovcara and that I saw there the JNA officer Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me please, how is it that you're familiar with the face of Cyrus Vance?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him from television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how long were you able to watch television in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We watched television almost until October or November, or 10th or 11th of November. I told you that we had no electrical power at the time, but we had a generator in the basement of our building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what TV stations you were able to watch? Was it Belgrade and Zagreb stations, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we watched the Zagreb television programme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see at around that time my client on Zagreb television in one of the reports borrowed from the Belgrade television?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at around that time you used to see Cyrus Vance on TV screens?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him because we had all been expecting some kind of an action of the international community. So we were interested in these individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I suppose that you were also interested in learning the reasons for the arrival of Cyrus Vance in the territory of the former Yugoslavia and for his mission there?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I realised that he was the UN envoy for the former Yugoslavia. He was sent by the secretary-general or somebody there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him there, when the weapons were surrendered, I assumed that he wasn't there alone, that he had some people accompanying him. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I really didn't pay much attention to it. I saw a group of people, among which I recognised Cyrus Vance. All of them stood near the limo that I described to you. All of them wore suits. So in that sense they stood out from the other people standing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to ask you. I know that you mentioned the limo previously. Do you remember what he was dressed like? Did he have a coat or a hat?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely I wouldn't have noticed them there because there was a lot of people standing there, but they stood out precisely because of the clothes that they wore and the vehicle that was there. That was quite an unusual sight. They all wore suits, and there was this great huge limo there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And among those people, you recognised the envoy of the Secretary-General, the UN Secretary-General, Mr. Cyrus Vance?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was on the 18th of November at around what time of the day, between 12.00 and 5.00?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- well, when the surrender of weapons took place, at the same time, so it may have been between 3.00 and 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Ms. Foro, if I told you that at this time Mr. Vance was in a meeting with Ante Markovic in Belgrade, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If what you're telling me is true, then probably I am mistaken or I'm simply mistaken about the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I told you that in this same chair where you are sitting now we had Mr. Vance's personal advisor. I asked him clearly what he knew about the surrender of weapons at Mitnica or whether he had heard anything about it. He said he knew nothing about that, nor was Cyrus Vance in Vukovar at all on that day.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified about what I had seen. You're saying something different, and it's up to the Chamber to determine what the truth is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you came here to testify under oath about the facts that you were familiar with and say everything to the best of your knowledge, everything with us.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that whenever you say something that is not truthful or you are not positive about, it is better to be clear about that and say that you're not sure as opposed to stating something with an appearance of certainty.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified about things that I personally witnessed. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now please have a break? Although this is not our usual time, but this is a logical rupture in my cross-examination. We have to up the ante, as they say, and use some other documents -- use some other documents. So we can now have a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: To accommodate your every wish, Mr. Lukic, we will have a break. We will resume at 25 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now continue with my questions in relation to, for the most part, to yesterday's testimony. Yesterday on page 29 of the working transcript, as we call it, you described how you moved along in that column, as you called it -- or, rather, let me not lead you on this. As you moved in that column of civilians around the cemetery, did you see the moment when the town defenders handed over their weapons or surrendered their weapons?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That happened at the cemetery. Our column of civilians reached the cemetery, and I noticed that the town's defenders, those who were armed members of the National Guards Corps, were laying down their weapons and the weapons were then taken by the JNA soldiers. This happened in the immediate vicinity of the road that the column was travelling on, the column of civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that the weapons were being laid down on the road, the same road that the column was using at this same time?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The civilians were walking along that road, and the soldiers were 2 or 3 metres off the road, not on the asphalt surface. And that was where they laid down and surrendered their weapons. You can see it in video clips and paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you said during your testimony today, the town's defenders had uniforms and insignia. Were they wearing their uniforms at the time when they surrendered their weapons?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified about the civilian protection. What about its members? Did they, too, surrender their weapons on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because they had no such weapons in their possession. They would only be given weapons when they were standing guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did say that, but you weren't clear about the time-line of the surrender itself; however, thank you for clarifying that point for me. You also testified that when they surrendered their weapons they were listed by a representative of the International Red Cross and an EC monitor. I think you said that today.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them standing nearby. They were monitoring the surrender of weapons and drawing up lists with people's names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a specific question. Did you see a piece of paper in their hands? Were they asking people their names, checking people's identities? Can you please describe the physical set-up of the situation at the handover of the surrender of weapons. What exactly did you see?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a representative of the International Red Cross and an EU monitor, I saw the fighters surrendering their weapons, and I saw this representative of the International Red Cross addressing each and every individual, each and every of those persons who were in the process of surrendering their weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand you when I say that this list of the International Red Cross list that was drawn up on the 18th of November is the list that you saw later on in Zagreb when you started working there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this list containing the names of 180 people who laid down their weapons, but I'm not sure that it was the same list that was drawn up at the time. I can't confirm this simply because I did not see the list at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I fully agree with that, but the one that you did see, was it marked in any way in order to show that it was drawn up by the International Red Cross? Did it bear a date perhaps, do you remember, the one that you saw later?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it had any sort of sign or distinctive mark, but we dealt with a great many lists. And it's possible that I never saw the original one put together by the International Red Cross. Maybe it was entered into a database later on and a printout was made or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there's no heading, no stamp, no sign of the International Red Cross. Do you remember seeing anything like that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you rule out as impossible the following suggestion, namely that the list was actually drawn up by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA had a lot of opportunities to draw up this and other such lists, since all those that surrendered their weapons were seen as prisoners of war and they subsequently ended up in prisons all over Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means that you can't rule this suggestion out as something that was impossible?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that they could easily afford to make a list, one list each day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again I'm asking: Can you rule my suggestion out as impossible? Please answer yes or no. Do you think that is impossible or may that as well have been the case?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've answered the question. It would have been quite possible. They could have made a list for every day they kept those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified yesterday that when you were there for the surrender of weapons you saw a person at Ovcara who introduced himself as Major Sljivancanin. You had the impression that he was the man in charge, to put it quite simply. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to show a video. I believe the witness has already seen this video many times, because based on what we know she had been shown this footage on many occasions. This is V0001-626. It's an OTP exhibit. This is a video clip. It's quite lengthy. It goes on for over 60 minutes, I think about 70 minutes. I'm about to show a sequence with no translation. I don't think it's material to this particular portion to have a translation. As to what I know about the transcript, I think the OTP has prepared a transcript for a different portion of that video that will later be tendered into evidence. I would like to play the video now, and please if the witness can state clearly whenever she recognises a face or a person in the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this please be assigned a number, this video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 124.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Foro, what about the this video? Does that seem familiar? Is this, in very rough terms, the same thing that you saw as you were passing along in that column?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you have just shown the very end of the process of surrendering weapons. The first to go were people who were wearing uniforms, as I previously stated, and those who negotiated on behalf of the National Guards Corps headquarters from Mitnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the negotiators the only ones wearing uniforms or were all ZNG members? There were over 180 people, ZNG members, there who laid down their arms on that occasion as members of the ZNG. Did you recognise anyone? Did a face seem familiar?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already seen the entire footage, which is over an hour long, and I did recognise people back then but not in this particular portion because the quality of the image is not that good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sure the OTP will probably be tendering the whole video. It really is quite long, and we shall see how many people there were who were in uniform. But I have this question to ask you: Did you at any point during this short clip see my client?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in the portion that you have just shown, that you have just played.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see a single frame in any one of these videos showing the surrender of weapons where my client could actually be shown?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about the footage that I have personally seen or are we talking about my personal experience there, what I witnessed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you if you have ever seen a video with my client in it at the surrender of weapons?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no videos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us what you personally witnessed, that's all right. But tell me: In this video, did you see a representative of the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in the portion just shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To avoid mistakes, Mr. Borsinger actually walks right through; there's this short sequence where we can see him. But did you ever see any video recording showing the International Red Cross representative making lists of people as people were surrendering their weapons?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this video I see many people with long hair and beards. Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the JNA people or the people surrendering their weapons?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume you know who I mean, don't you? I mean the people surrendering their weapons.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There weren't that many to begin with. There was no running water in Vukovar. It was very difficult to wash on a regular basis. None of them sported beards. Those were just unshaven individuals. I did notice, however, that the JNA people in this video did have beards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another thing that's important. Where did you leave your vehicle when you got there in relation to the HPV and those vehicles over there? Where did you leave your vehicles and did you leave the car keys on the front seat?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea where the administration building was. I'm not that familiar with that particular area. I was never there. I'd never been to the administration building. I know there are hangars there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in relation to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's next to one of the hangars in a flat area, a flat, open area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the vehicles there?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There must have been three or four columns of vehicles with five vehicles each, five or six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You gave a statement to the OTP in 1995 on the 14th of September, that's at least what the statement says. The statement was read back to you in a language you understand. It was back-translated for you.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you signed a copy of the statement that was taken down in English. Right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also familiar with the fact that the statement contained everything that you knew at the time to the best of your recollection and whatever you answered to the questions of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I heard this a while ago, but please confirm this, if you can. You went through this statement again with the Prosecutor the other day. You provided certain comments, additions, and amendments, corrections, to your previous statement, details that were erroneously recorded and certain additional comments that you made?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They asked me broader questions about certain details, and I answered to the best of my ability, answered the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that. But there are parts of your statement that remain and have not been amended, and you stood by those portions also when you talked to the OTP some days ago. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now read a very short portion from the statement for my learned friend Mr. Agha. In the English version, this is page 4, the last three ERN numbers are 333. It is the second-last passage. Very briefly. You talked about Mr. Sljivancanin's speech, and you go on to say -- and you read this again with the OTP some days ago: "Elderly women and women with children boarded one or two buses that set out. We who remained, because we were neither mothers nor elderly ladies, were told to get on the bus but without our men. We refused and remained standing there. Then we said that Major Sljivancanin had explained that we were all going in the same direction and that there was no reason for us to part ways. Major Sljivancanin and a few other soldiers started talking among themselves and finally allowed us to get on the bus." Do you remember stating something like that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this how it happened?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you gave a slightly different account yesterday, didn't you? I'll ask you specifically --

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: How different? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you testified in chief on page -- let us find the page, track it down. It's page 41, page 41 of the transcript. [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... "said that the men had to be separated from the women next and that we were all going in the same direction." [Interpretation] So it wasn't Sljivancanin who told you, it was someone else. But then you addressed the things that he had told you previously. Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, but I'm not sure what the point is. What is your question? What did I misstate?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's very simple. Who told you that the women and the men should go their separate ways, be separated?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Sljivancanin. He was giving orders. He was telling people what to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in your statement you said it was somebody else who had told you that. It was only after that that you turned to Sljivancanin with this problem because he had told you previously that you would all be going together in the same direction?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, you got that wrong. Major Sljivancanin said we would all be going together in the same direction, but after that he said that men were to be separated from the women and the women should get on that bus or those buses. And then people started commenting: Why on earth should we be separated now if it is really true that we are all going in the same direction?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you listen carefully what I read back to you what you said in 1990 [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what you stated in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think this debate has any sense. I said in 1995 the same thing I'm saying now, that Major Sljivancanin gave a speech and that in that speech he said we would all be evacuated to Croatia. After that, after the elderly women left and women with children left, he asked that women and men be separated. The comments were: Why should we be separated if he previously said we were all going in the same direction. That is what I said then and this is what I'm saying now. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I cannot excuse that. I have to go back to that. At the time you did not tell The Hague investigators then or a few days ago when you were looking over the statement with the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think in view of the precise detail that you want to raise, it would be fair for the witness to have a copy of what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're absolutely right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a statement in -- a copy of the statement in B/C/S. This part is highlighted in yellow. You went over that part with the Prosecutor a few days ago. The second sentence, please follow along. "We women who stayed behind, because we were not mothers or elderly women, were told to board the bus but without our men."

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. "We refused and kept standing there. Then we said that Major Sljivancanin had explained that such-and-such thing." So it would seem, on the basis of this sentence, that he told you that. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? From the sentence "we said" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it seems that from this sentence it can be concluded that he said that to you.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told us to get on the bus. He was issuing the orders. He was telling us what to do. Obviously in the translation, since it was being taken down in English, there was a misunderstanding of some kind. But in any case Major Sljivancanin was issuing orders. He gave the speech, and he was saying who should do what. He commented that Major Sljivancanin previously said that we were all going in the same direction and that there was no need in that case to be separated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not tell The Hague investigator that Major Sljivancanin had told you that you needed to separate. You didn't tell him that, did you? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In your testimony yesterday you said that there was a discussion after that between Sljivancanin and those paramilitaries, as you called them - I'm going to use that term - who were complaining why he said that you should go together. That's what you said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. There was a discussion. We didn't hear what was being said, but we could see that there was a discussion going on. They went off to the side, off from the group, and there was a debate going on. I don't know exactly what happened during the discussion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what you said. And then Sljivancanin came and told you that you should all go together, and then you all went on the bus together?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sljivancanin interrupted the discussion and ordered that we all board the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These paramilitaries, let me define them like that, then, as you said on page 42, were extremely angry.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were angry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to Sremska Mitrovica you didn't get any explanation - that's what you said yesterday - why you were brought there and not to Croatia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody saw it fit to explain anything to us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you also testified that what Sljivancanin told you was different from what he actually did. Is that correct? Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please reply just with yes or no. That is your conclusion because you didn't go where you were supposed to go, so that was your conclusion that he changed. What happened was not actually what he said?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't hear from anyone that it was his decision. This is something that you assumed based on your image of my client and the importance that you attached to him based on what you saw him doing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a person who introduced himself as a person who was giving orders in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer my question. We heard that already. You did not hear him say that the route would be changed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm sorry to interrupt, but in fairness that was a direct answer to your question. You asked: Did you assume? She said: No. Your client had introduced himself as in charge. That was, in her answer, her basis for the views she formed. Now, if you didn't understand that, fine; but if you did, what you went on to say was misleading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour. I think that her answers were actually quite clear regarding what I wanted to hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end, at Ovcara - I'm not talking about further developments - at Ovcara you actually boarded the bus together with your husband. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It all ended there at Ovcara when you boarded the bus in the way that Mr. Sljivancanin had previously told you - is that correct - that you would be going to Croatia together with your husband, and that applied to all?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how you mean. Going to Croatia is one thing and going to Mitrovica is another. It did not end the way the commander, the person who introduced himself as the commander, said it would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You boarded the bus with your husband, despite the loud protests of the paramilitaries as you were boarding it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We boarded the buses and the buses set off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is what I wanted to hear. You said that you worked in a state organ at the health ministry. During the days in Mitrovica or later when you had access to, evidently, important information, did you hear that convoys could not cross into the territory of Croatia in that period because the Croatian authorities did not want to admit them? Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear it in the way you are putting it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't have a problem with that. What do you say to my assertion that there was a TV programme broadcast on Croatian television about Vukovar yesterday and there was a conversation between Mr. Dedakovic and Tudjman played when Mr. Dedakovic requests Mr. Tudjman to have children and the elderly evacuated, and Tudjman literally replied to him that this was out of the question at that point in time. Would I be making a mistake if I were to tell you that this is what I heard on Croatian television yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know if you were making a mistake or not because I was not listening to Croatian television yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay at your post where you were working, did you ever hear any stories about the Croatian leadership in Zagreb being in favour of preventing Croatian civilians leaving the area of Vukovar when they wanted to?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I bring to the Chamber's attention that a number of these questions are speculative in nature, and, for example, about watching the TV, not really a question which the witness can adequately deal with or ought to be asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
