utterances.text: There is some substance in what you say, Mr. Agha, but the Chamber is watching that and in each case this witness is not put off or confused by being asked a question of that nature and she's dealing with it in a straightforward way. So I don't think we need to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to say that at no point was it my intention to confuse the witness. I wouldn't want anyone to get that impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Foro, in your testimony you said that you saw my client in a lot of places, that you heard that he was at the negotiations on surrender, that you saw him during the surrender near the cemetery, and finally that you saw him face-to-face and met him at Ovcara. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These facts are based on your recollection, also are based on the photograph that you described yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mostly talked here about the things that I saw when I was in Vukovar. I just mentioned that I saw a better photograph than the one we saw yesterday where you can also see Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to comment, but you didn't testify only about the things you saw but also about the things you heard. You said that he was present at the negotiations.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I always indicated when I saw something and when I only heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These photographs that you had the opportunity to see later -- this photograph, actually, and you said that you can obtain it, you remember that he was sitting at the table at the same place that Mr. Khan pointed out to you yesterday. And based on that you conclude that his hand is visible since you saw a better photograph with Major Sljivancanin sitting at that place?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the photograph, but it was taken from a different angle. So I cannot tell you exactly where Mr. Sljivancanin sat, but I think I indicated it. I saw a photograph which much better depicts exactly where all the negotiators sat, including Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's be precise. Based on something that you know, you said yesterday that that was his hand - is that correct - based on another photograph that you saw?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that I thought that was his hand, and if you excuse me I think that this is a major difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to -- and I'm sorry to interrupt here. But actually, the witness has very quite rightly pointed out that she assumed it was his hand and that is her belief, and that is very clearly mentioned in the transcript. It is not a question that she said it was his hand. And that's at page 24, and I can actually read you the part and the reply was: "So I assume that the hands we see there are his hands, although I can't be quite certain. Of course, on the other photograph I saw, I saw Mr. Sljivancanin." So I think it would be both unfair and incorrect to make such an assertion that the witness has actually said she saw his hands in her prior testimony when that was not in fact the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you've taken that on board, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. But it seems to me -- but -- well, it's the Prosecutor's right. With this line of questioning I would like to establish where Mr. Sljivancanin sat based on the photograph that the witness remembers. I just wish to confirm that she said yesterday that she thought that that was his hand, on the basis of the photograph from which she remembers his face well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, had I been present at the negotiations, then I would know exactly where Mr. Sljivancanin sat, all the other negotiators, the Red Cross negotiators. When you see a photograph from a different angle it always seems different and that's why I did say that I assumed that is where he sat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about this photograph where you say you saw the face of Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we in the meantime show the witness Exhibit 120, that is that shot that the Prosecutor showed you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Was Mr. Sljivancanin there in that photograph from which you remember his face? What was he wearing? A uniform? Was it a camouflage uniform? What kind of a uniform was it?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know definitely that he was wearing a uniform. I cannot remember whether it was a camouflage uniform or an olive-drab uniform, though it was probably a camouflage uniform; that is more likely. But I cannot remember exactly. In any case, he was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you remember, or am I asking you too much, what his expression was on his face? Was he serious? Was he smiling? Do you remember his facial expression on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was serious. I don't ever recall seeing his photograph in which he was smiling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what you remember with certainty from this photograph and what you testified about yesterday is that he sat at the table in the company of these gentlemen?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the photograph in which at the negotiations he was present and the other three negotiators also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the other three negotiators," you mean the negotiator from the JNA, from the ZNG, and the representative of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm thinking of the three negotiators from the Croatian side. Here you can only see Mr. Filip Karaula well in this shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You marked these other individuals whom you have recognised. My question was very simple and I don't think you answered it. What you show -- what you saw on that photograph were Sljivancanin and these people.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw on the photograph were three negotiators representing the Croatian side and Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were all sitting?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because yesterday you stated that you supposed that this arm that can be seen in the photograph was Mr. Sljivancanin's; that's the only reason I asked you that. Please tell me: Did you ever offer this photograph to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever asked me about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But yesterday you said that you could get -- gain access to that photograph and then deliver it to the court?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When the negotiators came back and when they reported on the success of negotiations, did they tell you what was the position of my client during negotiations? Did they tell you about what he had discussed, if anything?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to confess that at the time we didn't really focus on your client; he wasn't the most important person for us. Rather, we were interested in how to evacuate civilians from Vukovar and we were also interested in our fate. So this is what we focussed more than on your esteemed client.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I just wanted to see whether you had any recollections concerning this. Please tell me: Am I wrong in saying that photographs can be used as souvenirs but can also be used as evidence, proving certain events?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are now going to take a look at the second video clip from which the Prosecution took this frame that they used yesterday in their examination-in-chief. This is the part of that same video material, and I selected the portion which shows certain events. And I assume that the Prosecution will tender into evidence the entire footage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me when you see my client so that we can stop the tape.

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see this clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell us which frame do you want us to pause on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: Yesterday they talk about surrender of Croatian forces who are [unintelligible] in Mitnica. "UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: He said that it was not exactly surrendered arms. They want to speak about the way how -- how [unintelligible] situation. "UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: He said that we can only -- only that things that the -- are -- "UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: His army -- "UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: -- His army had said. "UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: He said that first when we speaking that it was not starting the [unintelligible] end of his -- it was not shutting the -- the -- between the [unintelligible]. "MR. BORSINGER: Can I make -- I need to explain to go through this -- our -- the presence of the ICRC here is only in relation with questions of humanitarian nature. We can also be here as a neutral intermediary between both parties, if both parties request us to be a neutral intermediary. So I would like both parties to have to think about the exact role they want to give us and you want to give us, and I think that if we proceed in this, I would suggest that it's without the presence of the press, and I suggest that if we continue this session, unless both parties want the press, I have no problem -- you prefer the press? "UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: He said that about this" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This goes on for quite a while and the Trial Chamber will have occasion to see the entire material. Could we be given exhibit number for this entire document that we just saw?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I be clear whether it's the entire film or just this part?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that right now it would be best to introduce into evidence just this portion. Later on, when the Prosecution is ready, I assume that they will tender in the entire footage with the transcripts from negotiations, which I think lasted for about 20 minutes. For the time being, let us just tender into evidence this portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 125.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please answer my question briefly. Did you see Major Sljivancanin in this clip?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam Foro, please tell me, am I wrong in claiming that Major Sljivancanin did not take part in negotiations, that he was not in command during surrender, that Mr. Vance was not in Vukovar on the 18th, that the International Red Cross did not sign or did not put any names down? Am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question: Do you remember clearly the oath or the solemn declaration that you took yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Before I move to re-examination, Your Honour, may I just kindly ask the witness to, if she has the transcript before her, just to be sure what her last answer was to the last question, which is at line 10, 13.30.28: Did she reply yes or no? I think it's page 92, line 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me assist. The witness said that I was wrong. She said that what I stated was wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Your claims were not correct. The question was: Am I wrong? And I answered: Yes, you are wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I just wanted to clarify that. Re-examined by Mr. Agha:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, during your cross-examination you mentioned that you reached the precise figure of 180 people who surrendered when you started working at the office of missing persons. Now, you yourself were personally present at the surrender, so from your own personal observation what, roughly, were the number of defenders who surrendered?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your question? Did I see the surrender or did I see what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you witness surrender and roughly how many fighters did you witness surrendering?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the surrender, the very beginning of it when they started surrendering weapons. I saw that there was a number of people in that column, in that line, between 150 and 200 people. That would be my estimate. At the time I didn't know that the exact figure was 180. I didn't count the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during your cross-examination it was also suggested that you did not go out and leave the basement very much. On what occasions would you briefly pop out of the basement? For example, for food or to the bathroom or for things of that nature?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in order to go to the bathroom we had to go outside and that was quite dangerous. A lot of people died while doing that. It's not something I like to go back to in my mind. We also went out once a week or once in two weeks, depending on what was going on, to go and visit my family house. And that varied, depending on the intensity of the shelling. It was very dangerous to go there, and on several occasions I almost got killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it was also suggested in cross-examination that when you went outside your powers of observation were not very sharp. How would you comment on that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, when you leave a basement where you are practically incarcerated throughout the entire time due to the shelling, so once you come out and get into the streets that are very familiar to you, once you find yourself in the neighbourhood where you used to live, then your observation powers are quite powerful. You notice everything. You see bodies blown to pieces by shells. You see the damaged houses, and you can hear the shelling quite well. The town looked like on the day after a nuclear catastrophe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, turning to a different area of your cross-examination it was mentioned to you that when you reached the hospital, you got to the hospital gates, you didn't go inside, and you were only able to see parts of the hospital. Can you tell the Chamber what parts of the hospital you were able to see, how much of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the gate one can see the entire yard and the hospital building, the facade facing the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what condition could you see the hospital was in from there?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see that it was quite damaged, that the window panes were broken, that the walls had holes in them caused by shells. I saw that the roof was damaged in the yard. I saw a lot of construction debris. All the things that had fallen off due to the shelling, bricks, roof tiles, and so on. I saw that that part of the building, the one above the ground, could not be used, was not usable. One could not house patients in that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what weapons did you see protruding from the parts of the building you could see and have just described to the Court in your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any weapons in the hospital. This is the third or fourth time I've repeated this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn to another area of your cross-examination, and this is quite recently where we started to look at some videos. And the first video learned Defence counsel showed you concerned the line or group of people surrendering at Mitnica and laying down their arms. And according to your evidence, only a portion of that surrender process was seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: So with the leave of the Court, I'd like to show a further portion of that video, and I believe it's of the surrender of Mitnica. And perhaps you could confirm whether you're able to recognise anyone in that part. And the video showed with V000-1686, and it has 65 ter 311 -- I'm sorry. That's not the correct 65 ter my case manager has kindly informed me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, could I have a five-minute break, please, if we're not bound to finish any time soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would normally finish in six minutes' time --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would normally finish in six minutes' time. Would you prefer a break now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I thought it would go on for much longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm just going to check. Mr. Agha, how do you see your schedule?

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: I will try and finish in six minutes, depending on the length of this video clip, which I haven't actually seen myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let's get on with it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: So it is the ter number 311 after all, my case manager has informed me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to see this video, Witness, the clip?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you inform the Chamber whether this is also part of the surrender at Mitnica?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the column of civilians moving along the road towards the new cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which representative is that?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the International Red Cross man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in fact he was present at the surrender, according to the video?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I kindly ask that this segment of the video be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 126.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for the record, it seems to be indicated by the learned Defence counsel that the OTP plays you thousands and thousands and thousands upon hours of videos. Could you kindly tell the Chamber how many videocassettes the OTP showed you and for how many minutes when you reached here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't object to the question, but I sincerely don't believe that any of the Defence teams suggested what the Prosecutor has said in the introductory part of his question. I don't think any of my colleagues or I have ever said anything like that, but I don't oppose his question as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Well, actually, for the record, Your Honour, you'll see when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Agha, get on. The witness would like to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after that video I would now like to turn to a different area of your cross-examination, and this is at Ovcara. Now, you mentioned in your evidence and also during cross-examination that there was a heated discussion between Mr. Sljivancanin and the paramilitaries before you were all allowed to continue on your way. Would it have appeared -- how angry would it have been apparent that the paramilitaries were? Would it have been apparent that the paramilitaries were angry with Mr. Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll repeat this. The paramilitaries and Mr. Sljivancanin walked away from that group and there was a debate, at least as far as I could see, what was ended by Mr. Sljivancanin. He ordered all of us to get on the buses, and I think they, the other party, were dissatisfied with this decision that he had made. Of course there is also what he told my husband later on. It's part of my statement, and that seems to confirm this previous statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, very briefly, turning to the second video which the Defence counsel showed to you, and I don't -- I won't show you that video, and also the question of the photograph where you believe that Mr. Sljivancanin was at that negotiations. Now, this photograph which you say you have seen, did it in fact have -- who was actually in it?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Major Sljivancanin in the photograph, alongside with three Croatian negotiators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if it were possible, would you be prepared to bring that photograph back to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to make sure I haven't forgot, did I ask the Chamber to exhibit the last video clippage of the ICRC. I believe I did?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Exhibit 126.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now back to the final question and that's regarding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just one small intervention in the transcript, Your Honour. Page 98, line --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. May I have a short break, please, a couple of minutes. That's all I need. It appears that we shall go on discussing this for some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Please leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, your transcript intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may as well use the break for that. Page 98, line 9 and 10, when she said she stated that the other man had told her husband what she described yesterday where the paramilitaries were, whereas based on the transcript we might conclude that it was Sljivancanin who said this. Because the transcript states "he," and she was describing that first man who said what she said yesterday, what her husband said about getting on the bus and her husband got on the bus. So that's the confusion I'm trying to avoid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We are over time, Mr. Agha. Clearly if you have only this one final issue ...

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Actually, there's two questions and they'll both be quite brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Although, Your Honour, after the witness has left there is a question I won't be asking to her, but I would like the view of the Chamber on it so as to save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not today.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Maybe tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are sorry to have embarrassed you. Yes, Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, coming back to Mr. Vance at the surrender. Now, the person who you think was Mr. Vance, did you personally go up to him and introduce yourself at the surrender?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't approach them. I saw them from the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, apart from the question of possible mistake about Mr. Vance, in all other respects would you regard your evidence of what you personally saw as being accurate?

utterances.speaker: SARLOTA FORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified about what I saw. I testified truthfully. My testimony is entirely truthful. I can't remember a single thing that I merely heard without explicitly indicating that. I am quite positive that I saw Mr. Vance there wearing a suit, accompanied by some other people who were also wearing suits. It was quite obvious to me at the time that he just arrived from some sort of meeting, an official one probably, in a limousine. I saw him there and I think I'm right in saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That completes the re-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mrs. Foro, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questioning and your evidence. You are at liberty, of course, now to return to your home. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance here and your assistance. We will now adjourn. 9.00 a.m., tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
